Step 1 (diagnose, verified against actual code, not the issue's prose): read lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's dispatch_start/4 (lines 212-222) directly -- it does `case Enum.find(definition_snapshot.edges, &(&1.source == node.id)) do nil -> {:error, {:unknown_node_id, node.id}}; edge -> ... end`, a defensive nil-branch guarding against a :START node with zero outgoing edges. Read lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex's CHK-04 check_isolated_nodes/1 (lines 389-435) directly -- confirmed it enforces 'every :START node has >=1 outgoing edge' but purely as a runtime validator call site; Graph.t()'s @type/struct shape carries no marker distinguishing a CHK-04-passed graph from an arbitrary hand-built one. The issue's technical claim is accurate. Ran `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test test/letflow/engine/`: 1 property + 19 tests, 0 failures -- nothing currently broken. Found the defensive branch already has dedicated coverage: transition_test.exs:257 'a START node with no outgoing edge at all returns a named error rather than raising (defensive totality)' -- so the gap this issue describes is purely static-type-level, not a runtime coverage gap.

DIAGNOSIS: (b) no code fix warranted now -- diagnosed-and-deferred, not resolved-by-code-change. Reasoning: REQ-044's REVIEWER gate already PASSed with this exact code; no test fails; CHK-04 does run before any graph reaches the engine in the current call path, so no invariant is actually violated at runtime today. Applying core-directives.md's anti-scope-creep norms and CLAUDE.md's 'don't design for hypothetical future requirements' directly: building the ValidatedGraph.t() wrapper now would itself be the scope-creep those norms forbid. It also fails ORCHESTRATOR.md sec 10's sizing checklist outright (adds a new public type/module/@spec; would change transition/3's @spec, which is asserted by existing tests) -- so unlike ISS-0020 it cannot be absorbed as a small in-run fix; it would need its own full WF-02-shaped design/implement/test chain with no requirement currently authorizing it.
